name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior Detection
description: Methods and tools (CooRnet, CooRTweet, VERA-AI Alert) for detecting coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network behaviour across Facebook, X and other platforms; this is the researcher's signature, continuously active line of work spanning elections, health disinformation and influence operations.

name: Platform Data Access & Governance
description: Research and expert advisory work on social media research infrastructure, API access post-CrowdTangle, the Digital Services Act / ECAT oversight, and platform content-moderation policies (e.g. Meta's political content reduction); addresses the methodological and regulatory conditions under which platform research is possible.

name: LLM-Assisted Computational Content Analysis
description: Development and validation of large-language-model pipelines (embedding models, judge-agent workflows, human-AI annotation) for classifying and analysing political and social media text at scale, a rapidly growing methodological focus reflected in recent publications and teaching.

name: Information Disorder & Health Misinformation
description: Study of disinformation narratives, fact-checking support tools, and the circulation of problematic health and political information across contexts including COVID-19, the war in Ukraine, and health content in India and Nigeria, underpinning projects such as PROMPT and MINE-FACTS.

name: Generative AI & Synthetic Media Manipulation
description: Emerging research on AI-generated visual and textual persuasion techniques used in coordinated disinformation and problematic promotional campaigns (e.g. gambling ads), and broader questions of countering disinformation in the generative-AI era, paired with a new graduate course on the topic.

name: Electoral Communication & Digital Campaigns
description: Comparative analysis of social media dynamics around national elections (Italy, Germany, Brazil, Australia), including coordinated account networks, political advertising, and citizen engagement with campaign content on Facebook and Instagram.

name: Political Polarization & Partisan Media Ecosystems
description: Investigation of partisan attention, insularity, and affective engagement in news consumption and sharing across Facebook communities, media parallelism, and cross-national newsfeed comparisons, central to the MINE programme's long-running agenda.

name: Social Media Platform Affordances & Engagement
description: Studies of how platform features (reactions, algorithmic governance, ad-targeting tools) shape visibility, engagement and audience behaviour on Facebook, including methodological work on using Facebook ads for survey recruitment.

name: Social TV & Second-Screen Audiences
description: Earlier but recurring strand examining Twitter-based audience participation around television programming and streaming platform launches, representing a foundational line of the researcher's work on networked publics.

name: Sociocybernetics & Digital Society Theory
description: Theoretical engagement with systems theory, sociocybernetics and the observation of social systems in the era of big data, reflecting the researcher's longstanding involvement with ISA's Research Committee on Sociocybernetics.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.

name: Survey Measurement Validity and Comparability
description: Papers examining methodological challenges in survey-based measurement, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how online sample composition and quality checks affect representativeness and response validity, and how question wording and dataset differences affect cross-national and longitudinal comparability of trust measures.
